name: Historic Street Surfaces Conservation Study and Guidance Manual — summary in Dublin City Heritage Plan review
publisher: Dublin City Council
specific_reference: Dublin City Heritage Plan 2002–2012 Review of Architectural Heritage Projects, pp. 28–29; study dated 2009 and supplementary 2010 setted-streets resurvey
notes: Council review describes a historic street-furniture and street-surfaces inventory and reports 27 streets with complete granite-flagged pavements, approximately 118 streets with surviving kerbstones, 37 streets with complete setted surfaces (including some modern reinstatements), and a 2010 resurvey identifying 78 streets/lanes. These are historical survey totals, not a current condition count; named streets and present survival must be checked before creating object records.

name: National Inventory of Architectural Heritage (NIAH) National Dataset — coordinate provenance
publisher: Department of Housing, Local Government and Heritage via data.gov.ie
specific_reference: Spatial Reference Systems and provenance metadata
notes: Dataset metadata identifies Irish Transverse Mercator (ITM, EPSG:2157) as the current spatial reference system and states that downloads include both Irish Grid and ITM coordinates to facilitate transition. It also explains that existing point centroids were digitised relative to OSI 6-inch mapping and that the older IG-referenced series requires revision against larger-scale ITM mapping. This is why converted points are source-derived and still require field checking.

name: TM65 / Irish Grid — EPSG:29902 and WGS 84 transformation
publisher: EPSG Geodetic Parameter Dataset
specific_reference: EPSG:29902; TM65 to WGS 84 (2), transformation operation 1641
notes: Defines the legacy TM65 / Irish Grid projected coordinate reference system in metres and its transformation to WGS 84. The published transformation accuracy is 1 metre; this does not establish the accuracy of the source NIAH point centroid.

name: Clontarf and Scots Presbyterian Church, Howth Road

name: Central Hall, 71 Clontarf Road, Clontarf

name: Clontarf Castle gate lodge, Castle Avenue, Clontarf
publisher: Department of Housing, Local Government and Heritage
notes: NIAH record for the Gothic Revival gate lodge built 1836–37. Records carved limestone, a corbel table with sculpted animal heads, carved stringcourses, hood-mouldings, a tower, former carriage arch, granite bollards and chain. Published Irish Grid reference 319498, 236289. Point locates the gate lodge, not individual carvings.

name: 86 Clontarf Road — NIAH registration 50030182
publisher: Department of Housing, Local Government and Heritage — National Inventory of Architectural Heritage
specific_reference: NIAH Registration 50030182; Regional rating; Architectural and Artistic interest; original and current use house; date 1845–1850; Irish Grid 319039, 236025. NIAH describes the 1847 terraced house, entrance details, granite steps and platform, cast-iron balustrade and railings, rear outbuilding and shared green.
notes: Primary official source for the property's identification, architectural description, appraisal, date and Irish Grid coordinate. NIAH states that the terrace was built in 1847 by Isaac Warren, steward of the Vernon estate, and that the group with outbuildings, former gate lodge and shared green remains a largely intact example of mid-nineteenth-century housing development. Coordinate transformation is documented separately.

name: Historic Street Surfaces Conservation Study and Guidance Manual — review summary
publisher: Dublin City Council, Dublin City Heritage Plan
specific_reference: Review of Architectural Heritage Projects 2002–2011, pages 28–30
notes: DCC review summarising its 2004 historic street furniture/surfaces inventory, 2008/2009 conservation study and 2010 supplementary survey of 78 setted streets/lanes. Explains the heritage significance of granite flags, kerbs, setts, coal-hole covers and gratings. Does not by itself identify a specific Clontarf object.

name: Dublin City Development Plan 2022–2028, Policy BHA18
publisher: Dublin City Council
specific_reference: Chapter 11, Policy BHA18 — Historic Ground Surfaces, Street Furniture and Public Realm
notes: Policy lists historic ground surfaces and public-realm features including milestones, jostle stones, ward stones, bollards, coal-hole covers, gratings, boot scrapers, basement lights, street skylights, water troughs, post boxes, lampposts, railings, stone kerbs, pavement flags and setts. Applies to Dublin City Council's administrative area only.
